text: Rule 1.1 Direct Purchase of Goods: Procurement of goods up to INR 25,000 on each occasion may be made without inviting quotations or bids on the basis of a certificate to be recorded by the competent authority. The Head of Department may approve such direct purchases subject to budget availability. Required documentation includes Sanction Order and Cash Receipt or Vendor Tax Invoice.

Rule 1.2 Purchase of Goods by Local Purchase Committee: Procurement of goods costing above INR 25,000 and up to INR 250,000 on each occasion may be made on the recommendations of a duly constituted Local Purchase Committee consisting of three members. The committee must survey the market to ascertain reasonableness of rates and obtain a minimum of three quotations. Approving authority is Dean or Associate Director. Required documents are LPC Constitution Form, Market Survey Report, and Sanction Order.

Rule 1.3 Limited Tender Enquiry: Procurement of goods estimated to cost above INR 250,000 and up to INR 2,500,000 shall be made by Limited Tender Enquiry (LTE). Copies of bidding documents shall be sent directly to not less than three registered or reputed suppliers simultaneously. The competent sanctioning authority is the Registrar or Financial Adviser. A tender evaluation committee must prepare a comparative statement.

Rule 1.4 Advertised Open Tender: For procurement of goods estimated to cost above INR 2,500,000, invitation to tender must be published on Central Public Procurement Portal and institutional website. Bids must remain open for a minimum of 21 days. The competent authority for approval is Director or Board of Governors. Mandatory documents include Open Tender Notice, CPP Portal publication proof, and Technical Evaluation Matrix.

Rule 2.1 Direct Service Engagement: Consulting, maintenance, or advisory services valued up to INR 100,000 may be engaged directly without competitive bidding, subject to approval by the Head of Department. Documentation required includes Service Order Form and Vendor Work Completion Certificate.

Rule 2.2 Limited Service Tender: Outsourced or non-consulting services between INR 100,001 and INR 1,000,000 require soliciting quotations from at least three pre-qualified service providers. Sanctioning authority is the Registrar. Documentation includes Scope of Work (SOW), Quotation Comparative Table, and Service Agreement.

section_path: Chapter 3 > Rule 3.1 Minor Civil and Electrical Works
text: Rule 3.1 Minor Works: Execution of minor repair, maintenance, or fabrication works costing up to INR 500,000 shall be initiated through quotation notices to at least three contractors. Approver is the Estate Officer. Mandatory records include Work Estimate, Measurement Sheet, and Completion Certificate.

Rule 4.1 Emergency Sanctions: In situations of natural disaster, medical urgency, or critical infrastructure failure, standard quotation procedures may be bypassed only with explicit written authorization and financial sanction from the Director. All emergency purchases must be tabled at the next executive board meeting.

section_path: Chapter 4 > Rule 4.2 Sole Source and Proprietary Purchases
text: Rule 4.2 Sole Source Procurement: Single source procurement from an original equipment manufacturer (OEM) or authorized distributor is permitted only when backed by a Proprietary Article Certificate (PAC) and when no equivalent substitute exists. Mandatory approval of the Proprietary Sanction Committee is required.
Rule 1.1 Direct Purchase of Goods: Under the 2020 guidelines, direct purchase without quotation was restricted to INR 15,000. (Superseded by 2024 regulations).
